paper_id: Li et al. - 2012 - Almost optimal dynamically-ordered multi-channel accessing for cognitive networks
title: Almost Optimal Dynamically-Ordered Multi-Channel Accessing for Cognitive Networks
motivation: In cognitive radio networks, the status of channels' availability and quality is difficult to predict and quantify; traditional MAB-based approaches fail to exploit multichannel diversity.
problem_framing: Formulate online sequential channel sensing/accessing as a Sequencing Multi-Armed Bandit (SMAB) problem where each sensing order maps to an arm.
key_insight: The ordering of channels with descending idle probability upper confidence bounds achieves maximum SCB, reducing storage from O(N^K) to O(N).
method_signature: Sequencing Confidence Bound (SCB) algorithm using channel-level instead of order-level statistics
evaluation_criteria: Regret in O(N^K log L) polynomial to channels and logarithmic to time; throughput improvement over baseline
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: UCB1 policy achieves zero-regret but performs poorly when number of channels is large, with exponential regret O(N^K log L)
evidence_for_taste: the rewards are no longer independent
learning process could be greatly accelerated
precise regret by this scheme is hard to achieve
thinking_moves: 把指数级order空间映射回channel级别统计，从而把O(N^K)存储降到O(N)
先证UCB1方法的指数级 regret 再提出改进
发现不同 sensing order 之间存在 reward 依赖关系
从 order-specific statistics 转变为 channel-related statistics
